Updated three specs for the `auto_dismiss_dialogs` → `auto_dismiss_dialogs_at_startup` rename: the cross-plugin trust-gating matrix in `agent-plugin-parity`, robinhood's unattended-settings list, and `single-claude-data-dir`. Same behaviour; the name now says when the flag applies.

Added `specs/claude-send-path-input-ownership/spec.md`, which documents why Claude Code dialog and shell-mode detection currently fails in any conversation with prior turns (the `^❯` input-prompt signal matches the transcript's echo of past user messages, not the live input box) and specifies the fix: classify dialogs and shell mode on their own evidence first, and ask whether the input box is present only of the bottom of the pane.

Implemented that spec. Claude Code dialog and shell-mode detection now works in conversations that have prior turns: the input box is identified by its position at the bottom of the pane rather than by a `❯` glyph that also prefixes every echoed user turn. `classify` recognises dialogs and shell mode on their own evidence before asking whether the input box is present, so a short dialog with a user turn echoed just above it is still found. Readiness became a predicate rather than a pattern, so it can fail when the pane is genuinely not ready. `ShellCommandPendingError` was removed: nothing caught it, and its wording already lives on the dialog it described, leaving one error for "something is holding the input". A readiness timeout no longer quotes the pane in the raised error, only in the log.

Added `specs/tmux-pane-lockdown/spec.md`: folds the tmux-lockdown findings into the send path for the harnesses driven through `send-keys`. A pane in copy-mode swallows `send-keys` while `paste-buffer` still works, so a pasted message lands in the input box and the Enter after it is eaten; and `session:window` resolves to the window's *active* pane, so one split silently delivers the message to someone else's shell. Both are fixed by storing the agent pane's ID in a tmux session user-option and clearing modes before every send. The spec also proposes carrying a machine-readable failure kind alongside the reason, so the workspace can withhold Retry when the pane is gone and only a restart can help -- mngr says what happened, the workspace decides which buttons that deserves.

Corrected that spec's harness scoping: codex and pi subclass `BaseAgent` directly and use none of the send-keys pipeline, so claude and antigravity are the only agents that inherit it and the fix needs no opt-in flag to reach exactly them. Added what Retry and Force are in terms of the behaviour they mirror, the queue rescue Force performs before restarting, and the one real obstacle to carrying a failure kind out of mngr -- `MessageResult.failed_agents` carries only strings, so a kind needs a channel that does not exist yet.
